examples.en: Our apartment building has city gas supplied.

examples.ko: 도시가스 요금이 이번 달에 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The gas bill came out high this month.
The gas meter reader came and checked the meter.
When you move, you should first apply for gas service.
The country house has no city gas, so it uses an oil boiler.
After switching to city gas, my heating costs went down.

explain: 배관을 통해 집으로 바로 들어오는 가스예요. 통에 담아 배달받는 가스(LPG)와는 달라요. 요금 고지서나 이사할 때 신청하는 일 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The city gas bill is high in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고지서 이야기에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing when talking about bills.

phrases.example: 이사 가면 먼저 도시가스를 신청해야 해요.
phrases.en: When you move, you must first apply for city gas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사할 때 꼭 필요한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something you need to do when moving.

phrases.en: We installed city gas in the new house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가스 배관을 집에 연결하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to connecting the gas pipes to a home.

explain_en: It is gas that comes straight into the home through pipes, unlike bottled gas (LPG) that gets delivered in tanks. It often comes up with utility bills and when applying for service as you move.

examples.en: I wiped my hands with a wet tissue at the restaurant.
I keep a pack of wet tissues in my bag.
The wet tissues dried out, so I can't use them.
There are separate wet tissues for babies.
Could you give me just one wet tissue?
I also put wet tissues in the car.

explain: 물에 적셔 나오는 티슈로, 손이나 테이블을 닦을 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '물티슈'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I wiped the table with a wet wipe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물휴지'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 물휴지, and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I wiped the child's hands with a wet tissue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로'를 붙여 닦는 도구로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-로' to show the tool for wiping.
phrases.en_equiv: to wipe with a wet tissue

phrases.en: Please give me one wet tissue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 요청할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Handy for asking at a restaurant.

explain_en: It is a pre-moistened tissue used for wiping hands or tables. In everyday talk people also commonly say '물티슈'.

en: to be lustrous; to be sheeny

examples.en: The wooden floor at home is so glossy that it's a little slippery.
I picked out a shiny apple.
There is a chair worn smooth and shiny by hands.
The pebbles have been washed by the river and are smooth.
I feel good when my new shoes are shiny.
My face is reflected in the mirror I polished until it shone.

explain: 표면이 매끄럽고 윤이 나는 모습이에요. '반질반질'과 거의 같게 쓰고, 반대는 '거칠거칠하다'예요. 큰 느낌의 '번들번들'은 기름기가 번지르르할 때 많이 써서 얼굴에 쓰면 좋지 않게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I picked up a smooth, shiny stone by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used as a modifier before a noun.

phrases.en: I polished my shoes, and now they're shiny.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 닦은 뒤의 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, for describing the state after wiping or polishing.

phrases.en: The newly bought pot is glossy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반들반들하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym that can be used almost interchangeably with '반들반들하다'.

explain_en: It describes a smooth, glossy surface. It is used almost the same as '반질반질', and the opposite is '거칠거칠하다' (rough). The bigger-feeling '번들번들' often means greasy-shiny, so using it about a face can sound negative.

en: to be foggy; to be murky

examples.en: It's foggy, so everything outside the window looks hazy.
My glasses fogged up quickly because of my breath.

examples.ko: 하늘이 부옇게 흐려서 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: The sky is hazy and gray, so it looks like rain.

examples.ko: 미세먼지로 멀리 있는 산이 부옇게 보여요.
examples.en: The distant mountains look hazy because of fine dust.
Everything was blurry in front of me, so I couldn't see well.
The window is fogged up and I can't see outside.

explain: 안개, 김, 먼지 때문에 흐릿할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '뿌옇다'는 더 센 느낌을 줘요. '부예요, 부예서, 부연'처럼 ㅎ이 빠지는 활용에 주의하세요. '부옇게', '부옇고'에서는 ㅎ이 그대로 남아요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 먼지 때문에 하늘이 부옇게 보여요.
phrases.en: The sky looks hazy today because of the dust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부연'은 '부옇다'가 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, ㅎ이 빠져요.
phrases.nuance_en: 부연 is the form of 부옇다 that modifies a noun, with the ㅎ dropped.

phrases.en: The mirror looks foggy because of the steam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'가 붙으면 ㅎ이 그대로 남아요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, the ㅎ stays.

phrases.en: I wiped the window, so it isn't foggy anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 부정할 때도 ㅎ이 남아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ㅎ also stays when negating with -지 않다.

explain_en: It is used when things look blurry because of fog, steam or dust. '뿌옇다' feels stronger. Note the ㅎ drops in forms like '부예요, 부예서, 부연', while it stays in '부옇게' and '부옇고'.

examples.en: My mother runs the household at home.
After getting married, I ran a household for the first time.
The husband keeps house and the wife works.

examples.ko: 살림하는 데 생각보다 손이 많이 가요.
examples.en: Running a household takes more work than I thought.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우며 살림한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since I started raising a child and keeping house.

examples.ko: 혼자 살림할 때는 장보기가 가장 어려웠어요.
examples.en: When I ran a home alone, grocery shopping was the hardest part.

explain: 청소·빨래·요리·돈 관리까지 집을 꾸려 가는 일 전체를 가리켜요. 한 가지 일은 '청소하다'처럼 따로 말하고, 살림하다는 전체를 묶어서 말해요. '살림을 차리다', '살림이 늘다'처럼 명사 '살림'으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My mother is really good at managing the household.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집안일을 능숙하게 한다는 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as praise for someone who runs a household skillfully.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 작은 집에 살림을 차렸어요.
phrases.en: The two of them set up a home in a small house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 집을 마련하고 함께 생활을 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when starting a new household together.

phrases.en: There are many stay-at-home dads these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살림하다'를 '-는'으로 바꿔 사람을 꾸며 주는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 살림하다 describing a person.
phrases.en_equiv: a dad who manages the home

explain_en: It covers the whole job of running a home: cleaning, laundry, cooking, and managing money. A single chore gets its own verb like '청소하다'; 살림하다 bundles them all. The noun '살림' is also common, as in '살림을 차리다' (set up a home) and '살림이 늘다' (accumulate household goods).

examples.en: The farmer tied the straw bundle tightly with a straw rope.
They say people used to twist straw rope by hand and use it.

examples.ko: 문 앞에 새끼줄이 걸려 있어서 궁금했어요.
examples.en: A straw rope was hanging at the door, and I was curious.
Straw rope is made from rice straw.
They tied the cow to a straw rope.

examples.ko: 새끼줄 두 가닥을 합쳐서 더 굵게 만들었어요.
examples.en: I twisted two strands of straw rope together to make it thicker.

explain: '새끼'만으로도 짚으로 꼰 줄을 뜻해서 '새끼줄'은 같은 뜻을 한 번 더 붙인 말이에요. 아기가 태어났을 때 집 앞에 거는 금줄도 새끼줄로 꼬아요. 매끈한 '끈'이나 굵은 '밧줄'과 달리 거친 짚 느낌이 나요.

phrases.en: Grandfather is twisting straw rope in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짚으로 줄을 만드는 일을 말할 때 '꼬다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '꼬다' (to twist) for making rope from straw.

phrases.en: I tied the bundle of firewood with straw rope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짚으로 만든 줄을 도구로 쓸 때 '새끼줄로 ~하다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '새끼줄로 ~' when the rope is the tool.

phrases.en: You need a thick straw rope to tie up the load.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄의 굵기를 말할 때 형용사를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an adjective before it to describe the rope's thickness.

explain_en: '새끼' alone already means a cord twisted from straw, so '새끼줄' adds '줄' to the same idea. The 금줄 hung at a doorway when a baby is born is also twisted from straw rope. Unlike a smooth '끈' or a thick '밧줄', it has a rough, strawy feel.

examples.en: Old documents are incinerated according to the rules.
If you incinerate trash, the amount shrinks a lot.

examples.ko: 시에서 폐기물을 소각하는 시설을 새로 지었어요.
examples.en: The city built a new facility that incinerates waste.
The secret documents were burned right after being read.
You must not burn fallen leaves as you please.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 남은 재료를 소각하지 않고 재활용해요.
examples.en: This factory recycles leftover materials instead of incinerating them.

explain: '태우다'보다 공식적이고, 쓰레기·서류·폐기물을 없애려고 태울 때 써요. 사람이 불을 붙여 처리하는 일에는 '소각하다'를, 저절로 불에 타는 일에는 '타다'를 써요.

phrases.en: We incinerated all the old documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 태워서 없앤 일을 공식적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used to formally report that something was already burned and disposed of.

phrases.en: Most of the collected trash is incinerated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피동 표현으로, 누가 태우는지보다 태워지는 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on what happens to the waste rather than who burns it.

phrases.en: I burned up the paper I wasn't using.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소각하다'와 뜻이 같지만 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 소각하다 but simpler and more everyday.

explain_en: It is more official than '태우다' and is used when burning trash, documents or waste to get rid of them. '소각하다' is for someone disposing of things by fire, while '타다' is for things that burn by themselves.

examples.ko: 생활 잡화 코너에서 수세미와 빨래집게를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a scouring pad and clothespins in the household goods section.

examples.ko: 설거지할 때 새 수세미가 있으면 훨씬 편해요.
examples.en: Washing dishes is much easier with a new scrubber.
I put dish soap on the scrubber and cleaned the pot.
The scrubber is so worn out that I need to replace it.

examples.ko: 이 수세미는 거품이 잘 나서 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like this scrubber because it makes good suds.
Grandmother washes dishes with a natural loofah.

explain: 요즘은 천, 철, 아크릴 등 재질이 다양해서 '아크릴 수세미'처럼 재질을 앞에 붙여 말해요. '식물 수세미'처럼 말린 열매 섬유를 가리킬 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: I wipe the dishes with a scrubber.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 말할 때 '로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '로' marks the tool being used.

phrases.en: Please change your scrubber often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡은 것을 새것으로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when replacing an old one with a new one.

phrases.en: I use a soft scrubber on the frying pan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성질을 나타내는 말을 앞에 붙일 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can place a descriptive word in front.

explain_en: There are many materials now, so people put the material first, as in '아크릴 수세미' (acrylic scrubber). It can also mean a natural loofah made from a dried plant, as in '식물 수세미'.

examples.en: We grilled and ate meat over a charcoal fire.
At the campsite, I lit the charcoal.
When making soy sauce, people put in charcoal.
Charcoal is used to remove smells.
Charcoal soot got on my hands.
There are also soaps made from charcoal.

explain: '숯'은 나무를 구워 만든 검은 연료이고, 불이 붙은 숯은 '숯불'이라고 해요. 한국 고깃집에서 '숯불구이'가 맛있다고 할 때 자주 나와요. '석탄'은 땅에서 캐는 연료라서 달라요. 발음은 [숟]이라 받침 'ㅊ'이 'ㄷ' 소리로 나요.

phrases.en: Please don't let the charcoal fire go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 붙은 숯을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to burning charcoal.

phrases.en: We're going to eat charcoal-grilled meat on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숯불에 구운 고기 요리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means food, usually meat, grilled over charcoal.

phrases.en: My father lit the charcoal in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숯에 불을 붙여 타게 할 때 '피우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 피우다 when getting charcoal to burn.

explain_en: 숯 is black fuel made by burning wood, and burning charcoal is called 숯불. It comes up when Korean grill restaurants brag about 숯불구이. 석탄 (coal) is dug from the ground, so it's different. It is pronounced [숟], with the final ㅊ sounding like ㄷ.

examples.en: I stuck the wrapping paper down with Scotch tape.
Could you lend me some tape?
I mended the torn paper with tape.
The tape tore off; where is the end of it?
I bought two rolls of tape at the stationery store.
Stick some tape on the corners of the poster.

explain: 원래는 한 회사의 상품 이름에서 왔지만 지금은 투명한 접착테이프를 두루 가리켜요. 줄여서 그냥 '테이프'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Please seal the box with tape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 줄여서 그냥 '테이프'라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life people often just say 테이프.

phrases.en: I stuck the photo on the wall with sticky tape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇으로 붙였는지 말할 때 '으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '으로' to say what was used to stick something.

phrases.en: I carefully peeled off the tape from the gift wrapping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙은 테이프를 뗄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for peeling tape off.

explain_en: It came from a company's product name but now refers to clear adhesive tape in general. People often shorten it to just '테이프'.

examples.ko: 식칼이 무뎌서 양파가 잘 안 썰려요.
examples.en: The kitchen knife is dull, so the onion won't cut well.
Mom cut the watermelon in half with a kitchen knife.

examples.ko: 식칼은 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep kitchen knives out of children's reach.
I bought a new kitchen knife and put it in the kitchen.
The handle of the kitchen knife has come loose, so it's dangerous.

examples.ko: 이 식칼은 고기도 생선도 잘 잘라요.
examples.en: This kitchen knife cuts both meat and fish well.

explain: 부엌에서 음식 재료를 자르는 칼이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '부엌칼'도 쓰고, 일상에서는 그냥 '칼'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '식칼을 갈다'처럼 '갈다'와 자주 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The kitchen knife is in the bottom drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '식칼'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the same meaning as 식칼.

phrases.en: I sharpened the kitchen knife on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갈다'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common partner verb is 갈다.

phrases.en: I cut the carrot with a knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 그냥 '칼'이라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life people often just say 칼.

explain_en: It is the knife used to cut ingredients in the kitchen. '부엌칼' means the same, and in daily talk people often just say '칼'. It often goes with the verb '갈다' (to sharpen), as in '식칼을 갈다'.

examples.en: The kitchen looks brighter after I laid a tablecloth.
The child spilled juice on the tablecloth.
I wash the tablecloth once a week.
Guests are coming, so I changed to a pretty tablecloth.
The tablecloth has a flower pattern, so it feels like spring.
The tablecloth is long, so it touches the floor.

explain: 식탁 전체에 까는 천이에요. 접시 아래에 놓는 작은 것은 '식탁 매트'라고 해서 달라요. '테이블보'라고도 많이 말하고, '식탁보를 깔다/걷다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I bought a white tablecloth for the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: '식탁보'와 같은 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Widely used with the same meaning as 식탁보.

phrases.en: I laid the tablecloth before the guests came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식탁에 천을 펼칠 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for spreading the cloth on the table.

phrases.en: The meal was over, so I took off the tablecloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깐 천을 치울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for removing the cloth.

explain_en: It is the cloth that covers the whole table. The small one under a plate is a '식탁 매트', which is different. People also say '테이블보', and you use it as '식탁보를 깔다/걷다'.

examples.en: I hurriedly stuffed my clothes into the bag.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 아무 데나 처넣으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not shove trash just anywhere.

examples.ko: 서랍에 서류를 처넣어 두니 찾을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: I crammed the documents into the drawer, so now I can't find them.

examples.ko: 배고파서 밥을 입에 처넣고 바로 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: I was hungry, so I wolfed down my rice and ran out right away.

examples.ko: 아무 데나 물건을 처넣는 버릇을 고치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to fix my habit of stuffing things anywhere.

examples.ko: 사기꾼을 감옥에 처넣어야 한다고 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: He got angry and said that the fraudster should be thrown in jail.

explain: '넣다'를 거칠게 말하는 느낌이에요. 정리하지 않고 마구 쑤셔 넣거나 억지로 넣을 때 쓰고, '감옥에 처넣다'는 화난 말투예요. 공손한 자리에서는 그냥 '넣다'를 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I shoved the receipt into my pocket carelessly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 대충 마구 넣는 거친 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a rough sense of stuffing something in carelessly.

phrases.example: 화가 난 그는 범인을 감옥에 처넣고 싶다고 했어요.
phrases.en: Angry, he said he wanted to throw the criminal in jail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화난 말투로 사람을 가두는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An angry-sounding way to talk about locking someone up.

phrases.example: 시간이 없어서 짐을 마구 쑤셔 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I had no time, so I crammed my things in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처넣다'보다 덜 거칠지만 비슷하게 마구 넣는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less harsh than '처넣다' but a similar picture of stuffing things in.

explain_en: It is a rough way of saying '넣다'. It is used for cramming things in carelessly or forcing them in, and '감옥에 처넣다' has an angry tone. In polite settings, just use '넣다'.
